plan.chapterName: Anton, Bivens, and Davis. Calculus, 10th Edition, Figure 14.6.7
plan.contextChunk: This figure shows a spherical wedge in 3D, the volume element used for triple integration in spherical coordinates. The wedge is a small solid (shown with orange, yellow, and green faces) bounded by six surfaces: two spherical shells at radii rho1 and rho2 (marked along the z-axis), two vertical half-planes at azimuthal angles theta1 and theta2 (shown in the horizontal plane near the base), and two cones at polar angles phi1 and phi2 (measured from the z-axis and indicated by arcs). The bounding surfaces are rendered transparently to reveal the wedge's position inside the overall spherical sector. The figure defines the spherical wedge as the three-dimensional analogue of the polar rectangle and identifies its six bounding surfaces in terms of the spherical coordinates rho, theta, and phi.

elements: z-axis drawn vertical with arrowhead and italic label 'z' at top
y-axis drawn to the right with arrowhead and italic label 'y'
x-axis drawn toward lower-left (toward viewer) with arrowhead and italic label 'x'

Large translucent light-gray spherical sector of radius rho2 spanning theta from 0 (x-axis) to ~90 deg (y-axis) and phi from 0 (z-axis) to 90 deg (xy-plane) — its outer spherical cap face is the pale curved surface at the right
Inner translucent spherical shell surface of radius rho1 (fainter curved arc surface nested inside the outer cap)
Two flat gray half-plane wedges lying in/near the xy-plane at azimuthal angles theta1 and theta2, running from the origin out to radius rho2
Two translucent conical surfaces at polar angles phi1 and phi2 fanning out from the origin

The small solid spherical wedge element bounded by rho=rho1, rho=rho2, theta=theta1, theta=theta2, phi=phi1, phi=phi2 — drawn with an orange near face, yellow inner/left faces, and a green outer spherical face
Vertical double-headed dimension arrow on the left labelled rho_2, running from the xy-plane up to a horizontal tick at height rho2
Shorter vertical double-headed dimension arrow labelled rho_1, from the xy-plane to a horizontal tick at height rho1
Two horizontal tick/leader lines at heights rho1 and rho2 meeting the z-axis
Long curved arc from the z-axis sweeping clockwise, ending in an arrowhead, labelled phi_2 (outer arc)
Shorter curved arc from the z-axis ending in an arrowhead, labelled phi_1 (inner arc)
Two small arrowed arcs in the xy-plane near the origin measured from the x-axis, labelled theta_1 (inner/short) and theta_2 (outer/long)
Origin point at the meeting of the three axes

interactions.teaches: that the six bounding surfaces are two nested spheres, two vertical half-planes and two cones, and that the wedge sits in the solid region where all six overlap

interactions.label: ρ₁ (inner radius)
interactions.teaches: the inner spherical face of the wedge slides along the ray from the origin; Δρ = ρ₂ − ρ₁ is the radial edge length

interactions.label: ρ₂ (outer radius)
interactions.teaches: the outer spherical face grows with ρ₂, and the wedge's area on that face grows like ρ², not linearly

interactions.label: θ₁ (deg, from x-axis)
interactions.teaches: one vertical half-plane bound: rotating it swings the wedge about the z-axis

interactions.label: θ₂ (deg, from x-axis)
interactions.teaches: Δθ = θ₂ − θ₁ stretches only the arc-length edge ρ sinφ Δθ, which shrinks near the poles

interactions.label: φ₁ (deg, from z-axis)
interactions.teaches: the upper cone bound; tilting it raises or lowers the wedge toward the pole

interactions.label: φ₂ (deg, from z-axis)
interactions.teaches: Δφ = φ₂ − φ₁ stretches only the meridional edge ρ Δφ

interactions.label: Edge lengths & volume formula
options: Show ΔV = ρ² sinφ Δρ Δφ Δθ
interactions.teaches: why the three edge lengths multiply to ρ² sinφ Δρ Δφ Δθ rather than Δρ Δφ Δθ
which single spherical coordinate is held constant on each of the six bounding faces (sphere ⇒ ρ const, half-plane ⇒ θ const, cone ⇒ φ const)

demo_steps.title: The spherical sector
demo_steps.narration: A translucent spherical sector of radius ρ₂ fills the first octant region; the colored wedge inside it is the volume element. Orbit to see it is a solid, not a flat patch.

demo_steps.title: Radial bounds ρ₁, ρ₂
demo_steps.narration: Pulling ρ₁ inward thickens the wedge between the two spherical shells: the radial edge is simply Δρ.

demo_steps.title: Azimuthal bounds θ₁, θ₂
demo_steps.narration: The two vertical half-planes swing the wedge about the z-axis; the edge they control has length ρ sinφ Δθ, so it shortens as the wedge climbs toward the pole.

demo_steps.title: Polar bounds φ₁, φ₂
demo_steps.narration: The two cones tilt the wedge up toward the z-axis; this edge has length ρ Δφ and is unaffected by θ.

demo_steps.title: The volume element
demo_steps.narration: Multiplying the three edge lengths gives ΔV ≈ ρ² sinφ Δρ Δφ Δθ — the Jacobian factor for triple integrals in spherical coordinates.

state.showEdges: Show ΔV = ρ² sinφ Δρ Δφ Δθ

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World scale: outer sector radius ρ₂ ≈ 2.6 units (slider up to 3.5); axes drawn from origin, z-axis up to +3.4, y-axis right to +3.4, x-axis toward viewer-lower-left to +3.2, each ending in a cone arrowhead with italic serif labels z (top), y (right), x (lower-left). Origin at scene center-left, roughly one third in from the left edge and 40% up from the bottom, matching the source. The big translucent sector spans θ ∈ [0°, 90°] (x-axis to y-axis) and φ ∈ [0°, 90°] (z-axis to xy-plane); its outer spherical cap is the pale curved surface facing right/front, color #DCDCDC at ~0.25 opacity with slightly darker silhouette edges #BFBFBF. A second, fainter shell of radius ρ₁ sits nested inside (same gray, ~0.15 opacity). The wedge solid occupies ρ∈[ρ₁,ρ₂]=[2.0,2.6], θ∈[18°,34°], φ∈[42°,60°] by default — placing it in the upper-right of the sector, just inside the outer cap, exactly as in the source. Wedge face colors: outer spherical face (ρ=ρ₂) green #7FB287 at 0.75 opacity; the near cone/half-plane faces orange #E89440; the inner/left faces yellow #EFD44F; edges drawn as thin dark lines #555. Half-planes at θ₁ and θ₂ are flat gray #C8C8C8 slabs from the origin out to ρ₂ lying near the xy-plane, visible as the two thin fans below-left of the wedge. Dimension arrows: vertical double-headed arrows on the LEFT of the z-axis, the outer one (label ρ₂, italic, to its left) from y=0 to y=ρ₂, the inner shorter one (label ρ₁) from y=0 to y=ρ₁; each terminates on a short horizontal tick that touches the z-axis at heights ρ₁ and ρ₂. Angle arcs: two arcs in the y-z plane starting on the z-axis and sweeping clockwise (toward +y), radii ~1.9 (φ₁) and ~2.3 (φ₂), each ending in an arrowhead at its angle, labels φ₁ and φ₂ set above the arcs near the top; the φ₂ arc is the longer outer one. In the xy-plane, two small arcs measured from the +x axis toward +y with arrowheads, labelled θ₁ (shorter, lower) and θ₂ (longer, above it), with short leader lines pointing to the corresponding half-plane. Volume factor: ΔV = ρ² sinφ Δρ Δφ Δθ; edge lengths Δρ, ρΔφ, ρ sinφ Δθ evaluated at mid-ρ, mid-φ. Enforce ρ₁<ρ₂, θ₁<θ₂, φ₁<φ₂ by clamping.
interactionPlan.notes: Build all curved surfaces with THREE.SphereGeometry using phiStart/phiLength (azimuth) and thetaStart/thetaLength (polar) so the sector and the wedge's spherical faces are exact; for the wedge build a closed BufferGeometry of six faces (two subdivided spherical patches, two flat cone-ruled patches, two flat half-plane patches) regenerated on every slider change. Use DoubleSide + transparent materials with depthWrite:false on the large gray sector so the interior wedge stays visible; render the wedge opaque-ish (0.8) and after the sector. Axis arrows: Line + ConeGeometry tips. All text (z, y, x, ρ₁, ρ₂, φ₁, φ₂, θ₁, θ₂, edge-length and ΔV labels) as CSS2DRenderer/sprite labels in italic serif so they stay upright while orbiting. Arcs via THREE.EllipseCurve or a small custom arc of points in the appropriate plane, with a cone arrowhead at the end. Click picking uses raycaster on named wedge faces; highlight the hit face and show a caption like 'φ = φ₂: a cone'. Keep default camera at a standard isometric pose so x comes toward lower-left, y to the right, z up.

authoredContext:
By a spherical wedge or spherical element
of volume we mean a solid enclosed between six surfaces of the following form:
two spheres (green) ρ = ρ1,ρ = ρ2 (ρ1 <ρ2)
two vertical half-planes (yellow) θ = θ1,θ = θ2 (θ1 <θ2)
nappes of two circular cones (pink) φ = φ1,φ = φ2 (φ1 <φ2)
(Figure 14.6.7). We will refer to the numbers ρ2 − ρ1,θ2 − θ1, and φ2 − φ1 as the dimensions of a spherical wedge.

discrepancies: Camera/orientation differs: the source places the y-axis horizontally to the right with x descending to the lower-left, giving a fan seen nearly edge-on; the generated uses a symmetric isometric view (both x and y descending), so the quarter-sector reads as a dome rather than the source's flat fan.

The coloured wedge is much smaller and less prominent than in the source — its six distinctly coloured faces (green outer, yellow inner, orange φ/θ faces) are not individually distinguishable at the default view, whereas the source shows a large, clearly multi-coloured block.
θ₁ and θ₂ labels are printed on top of one another near the origin ('θθ₂₁') and φ₁/φ₂ sit nearly adjacent, unlike the source where the four angle labels are well separated with long leader arcs.
The ρ₁/ρ₂ double-headed dimension arrows are compressed close to the z-axis and drawn with thin ticks, far less prominent than the large bracketed dimension arrows in the source.
The inner shell (ρ = ρ₁) surface is nearly invisible in the render, so the two-shell structure that defines Δρ in the source is not evident.
The θ arcs in the source are drawn as long leader lines sweeping out to the two half-planes near the x-axis; here they are short arcs with tiny arrowheads and the half-planes are barely visible.
evaluation.notes: Conceptually accurate and richly interactive spherical volume-element figure (six sliders, guided steps, clickable faces), but the composition is less faithful than it could be: the camera is more isometric than the source's y-horizontal view, the coloured wedge is too small to read its six faces, and the θ₁/θ₂ labels collide near the origin.

In the xy-plane, two small arcs measured from the +x axis toward +y with arrowheads, labelled θ₁ (shorter, lower) and θ₂ (longer, above it), with short leader lines pointing to the corresponding half-plane. interactionPlan.notes: Build all curved surfaces with THREE.SphereGeometry using phiStart/phiLength (azimuth) and thetaStart/thetaLength (polar) so the sector and the wedge's spherical faces are exact; for the wedge build a closed BufferGeometry of six faces (two subdivided spherical patches, two flat cone-ruled patches, two flat half-plane patches) regenerated on every slider change. Axis arrows: Line + ConeGeometry tips. All text (z, y, x, ρ₁, ρ₂, φ₁, φ₂, θ₁, θ₂, edge-length and ΔV labels) as CSS2DRenderer/sprite labels in italic serif so they stay upright while orbiting. Keep default camera at a standard isometric pose so x comes toward lower-left, y to the right, z up.

discrepancies: The coloured wedge reads as a single dark olive-green block with one orange face; the source shows a distinctly multi-coloured element (pale green outer sphere face, yellow inner/θ faces, orange cone faces) that makes the six bounding surfaces individually identifiable. Lambert shading plus the default light makes the faces too dark and too similar.

The wedge sits closer to the origin/z-axis and appears smaller relative to the sector than in the source, where it is a prominent element roughly midway out along the ρ₂ cap with clearly visible thickness in ρ.

The translucent supporting geometry is much fainter than the source: the grey half-planes θ₁/θ₂ sweeping down to the x–y plane and the shaded conical surfaces are barely perceptible, so the 'intersection of two spheres, two half-planes, two cones' reading is weaker than in the printed figure.

θ₁ and θ₂ labels are crowded together right at the origin on top of the x-axis rod, whereas in the source they are well separated with long leader arrows pointing into the x–y plane; the two θ arcs are also hard to distinguish at this scale.

Source shows clear tick/extension lines at the tops of the ρ₁ and ρ₂ dimension arrows spanning to the z-axis; the generated version has them but they are thin and the ρ arrows extend further left than in the source, slightly unbalancing the composition.
evaluation.notes: Correct spherical volume-element figure with the right camera, sector, dimension arrows and angle arcs, and a rich, pedagogically strong set of interactions (six coordinate sliders, guided steps, edge-length/volume readouts, clickable faces); main weaknesses are an under-coloured, too-dark and too-small wedge and very faint bounding half-plane/cone surfaces that dilute the visual resemblance to the source.

interactions.teaches: that the six bounding surfaces are two nested spheres, two vertical half-planes and two cones, and that the wedge sits in the solid region where all six overlap

interactions.label: ρ₁ (inner radius)
interactions.teaches: the inner spherical face of the wedge slides along the ray from the origin; Δρ = ρ₂ − ρ₁ is the radial edge length

interactions.label: ρ₂ (outer radius)
interactions.teaches: the outer spherical face grows with ρ₂, and the wedge's area on that face grows like ρ², not linearly

interactions.label: θ₁ (deg, from x-axis)
interactions.teaches: one vertical half-plane bound: rotating it swings the wedge about the z-axis

interactions.label: θ₂ (deg, from x-axis)
interactions.teaches: Δθ = θ₂ − θ₁ stretches only the arc-length edge ρ sinφ Δθ, which shrinks near the poles

interactions.label: φ₁ (deg, from z-axis)
interactions.teaches: the upper cone bound; tilting it raises or lowers the wedge toward the pole

interactions.label: φ₂ (deg, from z-axis)
interactions.teaches: Δφ = φ₂ − φ₁ stretches only the meridional edge ρ Δφ

The coloured wedge is much smaller and less prominent relative to the sector than in the source, and only the green (ρ=ρ₂) and orange (φ=φ₂) faces read clearly — the yellow θ-faces that are visible in the source are essentially hidden at the default view.
The φ₁/φ₂ arcs are drawn close to / inside the grey sector rather than sweeping well outside it with long clean leader arrows as in the source, reducing the clarity of the angle annotations.

θ arc radii are inverted relative to the source (θ₁ drawn on the larger radius, θ₂ on the smaller), and the θ₁ label sits nearly on the x-axis arrowhead rather than clearly between origin and the half-plane.
Extra grey structure not in the source: explicit rim lines and latitude/longitude grid lines on the shells and cones make the figure busier than the smooth translucent surfaces of the original.
evaluation.notes: A genuinely 3D, conceptually correct spherical volume-element figure with excellent interactivity (six parameter sliders, surface-visibility cycling, edge/volume readouts, clickable faces, guided steps), but the default camera flattens the x-axis so the θ annotations are cramped and the coloured wedge reads smaller and less dominant than in the source.
